long_biography.plain_text:
As a teenager, Eric Smidt travelled alone to Asian factories to negotiate directly with manufacturers, an experience that shaped Harbor Freight's product model. Cutting out intermediary resellers allowed the company to control specifications and pricing while building long-term supplier relationships.

Harbor Freight later brought more product development inside the business. Engineers and industry specialists design, test and refine tools sold under exclusive brands. Smidt extended that practical focus through Harbor Freight Tools for Schools, which supports welding, automotive, construction and other skilled-trades teaching in American public high schools. The programme also recognises instructors whose classes prepare students for skilled-trades careers.
